Yes. DR2 gives a 1-sigma error for the stellar velocity dispersion in the column `SIGMA_STARS_PRIME_err`, in km/s. It sits next to `SIGMA_STARS_PRIME`. The gas dispersion has the same pair, `SIGMA_GAS_PRIME` and `SIGMA_GAS_PRIME_err`.

Both sources list it: the ESO release description (the column table) and the VizieR ReadMe (`e_sigma*`, bytes 80–87). Neither says how the error was derived. The VizieR range for it is 0 to 4.7e+12 km/s, so some errors are huge and flagged values are possible. Filter those before using the column.

I did not open the FITS table itself, because `astropy` isn't installed in the system Python.
